item.lead:
You have the sorted character list and the two tables, stoi and itos. Now two small functions put them to work: one turns a string into ids, the other turns ids back into a string.

Run the cells and follow 'hi' through each step. You will also see what happens with a character the tables never learned.
item.follow: The round trip works because itos is the exact reverse of stoi. It only works for characters in the list, and the real list has 65 of them. Next, the encoded text gets cut into a training part and a validation part.

text_to_try = 'hi'

stoi = {ch: i for i, ch in enumerate(chars)}   # character -> id
itos = {i: ch for i, ch in enumerate(chars)}   # id -> character
print(chars)
print(stoi)
print(itos)"},{"cell_type":"markdown","id":"c3","metadata":{},"source":"`encode` looks up each character of the string in `stoi` and collects the ids in a list. `decode` looks up each id in `itos` and joins the characters into one string."},{"cell_type":"code","id":"c4","metadata":{},"outputs":[],"execution_count":null,"source":"def encode(s):
    return [stoi[c] for c in s]          # string -> list of ints

def decode(l):
    return ''.join([itos[i] for i in l]) # list of ints -> string

ids = encode(text_to_try)
print(ids)          # one id per character: 2 ids for 'hi'
